meetings.title: Brightline Retail: check-in
segments: Hi Olivia, can you hear us?
Yes, hi Tom. Hi Maya, nice to finally meet you.
You too, Olivia. Thanks for making time, especially after last week.
Olivia, thanks for making time.
Maya wanted to join personally, after the delay last week.
First, I want to apologize properly.
Your team was the one who told us ingest was stuck, and the first reply you got from us was vague.
That's not the experience you should have had.
What we've changed since: we added alerting that would have caught the delay within minutes, and we're changing how we run database changes so it can't happen the same way again.
That's reassuring. And to be fair, your team was responsive once they knew.
It was the first few hours that were frustrating, when we weren't sure anyone was looking.
That's exactly what we're fixing on the communication side too.
Would it have helped to have a status page you could check yourselves?
Yes, honestly. Even a simple page saying 'ingest delayed, no data lost, next update at two o'clock' would have saved us a lot of anxiety and a few emails.
That's on our list. It'll be part of the new incident process.
I appreciate you saying that.
Honestly, the delay itself was annoying, but it's not the main issue for us.
What is the main issue?
The tagging. We turned auto-tagging off for our support team about two months ago.
The tags felt random. Billing issues tagged as shipping, that kind of thing.
So now my team exports everything and sorts it by hand, which is exactly what we bought your product to avoid.
How many people are sorting by hand today?
Two people, for about half a day each week.
Plus me, reading through the summary they produce.
It works, but it's the kind of work I really don't want my team spending time on.
And when the tags were on, what was the worst part?
That we couldn't tell which tags to trust.
If some are wrong, you have to check all of them, and then what's the point.
It only takes a few bad ones to lose trust in all of them.
That's exactly what we've heard from other customers too.
When did you first notice the tags getting worse?
Was it gradual or sudden?
Gradual. About six months ago we launched a new returns process, and the tags just never caught up.
Everything about returns ended up as 'shipping', because the words overlap.
It got worse every month after that.
That's a really useful clue for the audit.
The rules probably predate the returns process.
That's really useful to hear directly.
I'll be honest with you both.
Our renewal is in about three months, and I'm being asked whether we should look at alternatives.
One of the AI tools pitched us last month.
Can I ask what the alternative is promising?
AI themes, basically. A weekly list of what customers are talking about.
The demo looked good, but they couldn't show me how it would work on our data, and it was priced per seat, which is expensive for a team our size.
Is there anything that would make the renewal conversation easier for you internally?
Evidence. If I can show my VP that the tags are better, or that the new themes found something real, that's all I need. Numbers beat promises.
Then let's make sure you have numbers.
Tom will include before and after accuracy in the audit summary.
Thank you for being straight with us.
Can I show you something early?
We've been working on a new theme clustering model, and it's a big step up from the old tagger.
It groups feedback into themes automatically, and you can merge or split them if they're wrong.
How accurate is it? That's really the only question I care about, after the tagging.
Honest answer: better than the old tagger by a wide margin, but not perfect.
Today, about four out of five comments land in the right theme.
That's why you can merge and split themes, and every correction improves it.
Four out of five is a lot better than what we have.
And I like that we can fix it ourselves.
This is much closer to what I actually need.
Can my team use this?
Not quite yet. We're planning a private beta with a small group of design partners.
I'd like Brightline to be one of them, if you're open to it.
Retail is exactly where we need more data.
What would being a design partner involve for us?
A thirty minute check-in each week with us, a shared channel for questions, and honest feedback.
In return, you get early access, free during the beta, and a real say in how it works.
That's reasonable. I'd want one of my two analysts involved, since they'd be using it every day.
That's ideal, actually. The people doing the work are the ones who'll tell us what's wrong.
Would we have to share our data with other design partners, or anything like that?
No, never. Your data stays in your workspace.
What we learn is how people use the product, like which themes they merge or split.
Never the content of your feedback with anyone else.
And if we join, how much time would it take from my analysts each week?
About an hour. The thirty minute check-in, plus a bit of time using it for real.
Honestly, if it works, it should save them far more than an hour.
That's an easy trade, if it works.
Good. That would have been a deal breaker for our legal team.
I'd be interested. It would change the renewal conversation for sure.
In the meantime, I don't want you sorting by hand for three months.
Let me have our support team audit your tagging rules this week.
I suspect some of the rules are misconfigured, which would explain the shipping and billing mix-ups.
How long would the audit take?
A couple of days. We'll look at the rules, compare them to a sample of your recent tickets, and fix anything misconfigured.
I'll send you a summary of what we changed, so your team knows why the tags look different.
And Olivia, if the audit finds something embarrassing on our side, we'll tell you plainly. No spin.
I appreciate that. Honestly, that's the difference between a vendor and a partner.
Then let's be a partner.
I'll send the summary by the end of the week, and let's book the next check-in for after you've seen it.
Sounds good. Thanks both, this was genuinely helpful.
Okay. If the tags get noticeably better, I'll turn them back on for a trial.
Olivia, is there anything else we should know before the audit starts?
Any categories that matter most?
Billing and delivery. Those are the two areas our executives ask about every week.
If those tags are right, we'd trust the rest much more.
Then we'll start with billing and delivery, and report on those two first.
That would help. Thank you.
I'll add Brightline to the design partner shortlist and schedule the tagging audit.
When would the beta start, roughly?
We're finalizing the plan next week.
I'll let Tom share the timing as soon as it's locked, rather than guess now.
That's fine. Honestly, this call changed my view.
I came in expecting to tell you we're evaluating alternatives, and I'm leaving with a reason to wait.
That means a lot. We'll make sure it's worth it.
